gaps.what: None of this project's own tests were run, because there are none this tool can find.
gaps.why: This project has no test script, so there is no suite to harvest journeys from. A test suite is the only source that walks this product with the arguments somebody actually thought about, so without one the check compares what it can read and call for itself, and no more.
gaps.unlockedBy: Point the project at vitest or Node's own test runner and every test file becomes a journey, run twice on each build and compared.

gaps.what: 1 journey could not be compared, because the build on record as working never got the product to do anything there: ask the server for GET /about.
gaps.why: Everything this build did on those journeys is new coverage, not a change: there is nothing on the old build's side of it. Reported as findings until 2026-08-31, which is how a product that started working came back as a pile of regressions nobody had caused.
gaps.unlockedBy: Ship once from a run in which these journeys actually ran, and they become part of what "working" means.

summary: 1 thing behaves differently, checked against 1.0.0, run live. 3 of 4 journeys had anything on the old build's side to be compared against; the other 1 was not compared at all, and is named in the coverage list. Running the new build twice showed 0 addresses that will not sit still, and 51 that do. 0 differences landed on the unsteady ones and were dropped; 4 remain. Nothing that used to be steady has become unpredictable. Everything reported here was re-checked against the old build booted live, so none of it is drift. What is NOT reported rests on the stored record from the last time the old build ran — a difference the store never captured cannot show up in this list. NOT EVERYTHING WAS CHECKED: 4 of the 4 ways into this product have never been walked through, so nothing here says anything about them, and 8 other things were not looked at (None of this project's own tests were run, because there are none this tool can find, and more). A clean result only covers what was walked — `staysfixed coverage` has the whole list.
